title: Trading Policy
date_approved: Approved by the AMP Limited Board

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: A director of any AMP Group Company. AMP Limited directors (other than the CEO) are Designated Persons under section 2.1.1, and directors of each main subsidiary under 2.1.4. Directors of AMP Limited are additionally subject to the absolute margin lending ban in 2.7, notification of their trading intention to the Chairman of the Board, and notification of changes in notifiable interests within 3 business days.

tiers.name: members of the Executive Committee
tiers.description: Members of the AMP Executive Committee. Their direct reports are Designated Persons under section 2.1.3, and each ExCo member may nominate additional Employees as Designated Persons. ExCo members share the Directors' absolute prohibition on margin lending arrangements over or in respect of AMP Securities.

tiers.name: Designated Persons
tiers.description: AMP Limited directors (other than the CEO); the CEO and their direct reports; the direct reports of each Executive Committee member; the directors of each main subsidiary (AMP Bank Limited, N.M. Superannuation Proprietary Limited and any other so designated); the company secretaries of AMP Limited and of each main subsidiary; and any other Employee specifically nominated by an Executive Committee member. Subject to black-out periods, prior notification, short term trading and short selling bans.

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: Any full time, part time or casual employee of any AMP Group Company and any contractor of, or secondee to, an AMP Group member. Bound by the insider trading rules and the section 1.7 Share Plan hedging ban, but not by black-out periods, notification, short term trading or short selling restrictions unless also a Designated Person.

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: As defined in AASB 124. Named only in section 1.7, which records the Corporations Act prohibition on KMP and their closely related parties hedging unvested equity remuneration or vested equity subject to holding locks.

tiers.name: Close Associates
tiers.description: A family member who may be expected to influence, or be influenced by, the Designated Person (spouse, partner, dependent children, dependents), and a company, trust, investment account or other vehicle the Designated Person or their Close Associate controls or has significant influence over. Designated Persons must take appropriate steps to ensure Close Associates only Trade where the Designated Person could. Carve-out where the Close Associate trades in the ordinary course of their professional capacity and not for the benefit of themselves or the Designated Person.

definitions.hedging_definition: Directors and Employees must not use any hedging arrangements in relation to shares, options, share rights and performance rights (whether vested or unvested) (Equity Instrument) held in a Share Plan. This prohibition ceases to apply in respect of any Equity Instrument acquired through a Share Plan from the time it is withdrawn from the plan, converted to an ordinary AMP share or converted to cash (whichever is the earliest).

windows.start_anchor: close of trading on the ASX on 15 June
windows.end_anchor: open of trading on the ASX on the trading day after the release of AMP's half year results to ASX

windows.start_anchor: close of trading on the ASX on 15 December
windows.end_anchor: open of trading on the ASX on the trading day after the release of AMP's yearly results to ASX

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The AMP Limited Board or AMP Limited's Market Disclosure Committee may specify any other black-out period from time to time. Not confidential to the affected population: AMP will provide Directors and Employees covered by section 2.1 with email notification of any additional black-out periods.

rules.detail: Entering into any derivative instrument over AMP shares is expressly an example of Trading, and AMP Securities expressly include derivatives entered into with a third party over or in relation to AMP shares, so OTC puts and calls with a bank are squarely covered. A Designated Person must notify the Head of Corporate Governance in writing at least 2 business days before, effect the trade on the second to fifth business day after notification, stay outside black-out periods and hold no Inside Information.
rules.evidence: entering into any derivative instrument over AMP shares ... derivatives entered into with a third party over or in relation to any of the above Securities.

rules.detail: No venue distinction is drawn; exchange-traded options over AMP shares are treated identically to OTC derivatives, subject to the same notification, black-out, short selling and 30 day short term trading rules.
rules.evidence: entering into any derivative instrument over AMP shares, and ... agreeing to do any of the above things.

rules.detail: A derivative used to hedge an Equity Instrument held in a Share Plan is caught by the absolute hedging prohibition in 1.7, which applies to all Directors and Employees regardless of Designated Person status and regardless of vesting.
rules.evidence: Directors and Employees must not use any hedging arrangements in relation to shares, options, share rights and performance rights (whether vested or unvested) (Equity Instrument) held in a Share Plan.

rules.detail: Vested Equity Instruments that remain held in a Share Plan (for example subject to a holding lock) cannot be hedged with derivatives until they are withdrawn from the plan, converted to an ordinary AMP share or converted to cash. For KMP the Corporations Act imposes the same result independently.
rules.evidence: In addition, the Corporations Act prohibits Key Management Personnel (and their closely related parties) from hedging unvested equity remuneration or vested equity subject to holding locks.

rules.detail: Absolute ban on any hedging arrangement over unvested shares, options, share rights and performance rights held in a Share Plan, applying to every Director and Employee. Breach may lead to forfeiture of Equity Instruments and, in serious cases, termination.
rules.evidence: Directors and Employees must not use any hedging arrangements in relation to shares, options, share rights and performance rights (whether vested or unvested) (Equity Instrument) held in a Share Plan.

rules.detail: The ban runs on vested Equity Instruments for as long as they are held in a Share Plan; it lifts only on the earliest of withdrawal from the plan, conversion to an ordinary AMP share, or conversion to cash.
rules.evidence: This prohibition ceases to apply in respect of any Equity Instrument acquired through a Share Plan from the time it is withdrawn from the plan, converted to an ordinary AMP share or converted to cash (whichever is the earliest).

rules.detail: Once shares are withdrawn from the Share Plan or converted to ordinary AMP shares, the hedging prohibition expressly ceases. Hedging those shares is then an ordinary Trade in AMP Securities: outside a black-out period, with prior written notification to the Head of Corporate Governance, no Inside Information, and subject to the direction and conditions power in 2.4.
rules.evidence: This prohibition ceases to apply in respect of any Equity Instrument acquired through a Share Plan from the time it is withdrawn from the plan, converted to an ordinary AMP share or converted to cash (whichever is the earliest).

rules.detail: An Employee who is not a Designated Person and holds AMP shares outside a Share Plan is not restricted from hedging by this policy; only the insider trading prohibition and the 'can we / should we' reputational test in 1.4 apply.
rules.evidence: This prohibition ceases to apply in respect of any Equity Instrument acquired through a Share Plan from the time it is withdrawn from the plan, converted to an ordinary AMP share or converted to cash (whichever is the earliest).

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar structure is Trading because it involves granting or disposing of a beneficial interest in AMP shares or a right to dispose of them, and because AMP Securities include derivatives entered into with a third party, so the 2.4 notification and black-out rules apply. If it is held in a Share Plan the 1.7 hedging ban bites first.
rules.evidence: granting, acquiring or disposing of any beneficial interest in AMP shares (or any option or other right to acquire or dispose of AMP shares)

rules.detail: Outright ban, defined narrowly as selling borrowed financial products with a view to repurchasing them later at a lower price. A cash-settled short derivative position is not obviously within that definition, but would still be Trading requiring notification.
rules.evidence: Short selling of AMP Securities by Designated Persons is prohibited.

rules.detail: Section 2.9 is confined to Designated Persons; the policy is silent on short selling by other Employees.

Securities lending is not addressed. Borrowing is mentioned only in the descriptive definition of short selling in 2.9; lending out AMP shares is not prohibited or named, though a transfer of beneficial interest would be Trading.

CFDs are not named but are derivatives entered into with a third party in relation to AMP shares and so AMP Securities; trading them requires 2.4 notification and falls outside black-out periods, and in practice the 30 day short term trading ban in 2.8 would prevent most CFD activity.
rules.evidence: derivatives entered into with a third party over or in relation to any of the above Securities.

rules.detail: Absolute ban for AMP Limited directors on entering into or maintaining any margin lending arrangement over or in respect of AMP Securities. The ban is on maintaining as well as entering, so pre-existing arrangements must be unwound, and there is no approval or exceptional circumstances route out of 2.7.
rules.evidence: Directors of AMP Limited and members of the Executive Committee are prohibited from entering into or maintaining any margin lending arrangement over or in respect of AMP Securities.

rules.detail: Same absolute ban as for AMP Limited directors, covering entering into and maintaining any margin lending arrangement over or in respect of AMP Securities.
rules.evidence: Directors of AMP Limited and members of the Executive Committee are prohibited from entering into or maintaining any margin lending arrangement over or in respect of AMP Securities.

rules.detail: Designated Persons who are not AMP Limited directors or Executive Committee members are warned against, but not prohibited from, margin lending over or in respect of AMP Securities. The warning is grounded in forced sale risk during a black-out period, and the policy states clearance to sell in a black-out period to meet a margin lending arrangement would not likely be granted.
rules.evidence: AMP warns all other Designated Persons against entering into or maintaining any margin lending arrangement over or in respect of AMP Securities due to the risk of forced sale of those Securities during a black out period, in breach of this policy.

rules.detail: Section 2.7 sits within the additional restrictions for Designated Persons; Employees who are not Designated Persons are not addressed.

Granting security over AMP shares is not named, but granting a beneficial interest in AMP shares, or a right to dispose of them, is an express example of Trading, so a share mortgage or charge in favour of a bank should be notified under 2.4 and taken outside a black-out period. For AMP Limited directors and ExCo members an encumbrance that forms part of a margin lending arrangement is prohibited outright by 2.7.
rules.evidence: granting, acquiring or disposing of any beneficial interest in AMP shares (or any option or other right to acquire or dispose of AMP shares)

rules.detail: The policy does not address the use of unvested Share Plan entitlements as collateral; in practice they are unable to be dealt with while held in the plan and any risk-reducing arrangement over them is caught by the 1.7 hedging ban.

Only margin lending arrangements are expressly banned, but the wording 'over or in respect of AMP Securities' is broad enough to capture a bank loan secured on AMP shares with lender protection against price falls. Other forms of secured financing are not separately addressed and there is no general secured financing clause.
rules.evidence: prohibited from entering into or maintaining any margin lending arrangement over or in respect of AMP Securities.

rules.detail: Identical prohibition to AMP Limited directors; no waiver mechanism is provided and section 3 exceptional circumstances relief is directed at black-out period trading, not at 2.7.
rules.evidence: Directors of AMP Limited and members of the Executive Committee are prohibited from entering into or maintaining any margin lending arrangement over or in respect of AMP Securities.

rules.detail: For other Designated Persons the policy contains only a warning, not a prohibition, on margin lending, and says nothing about other secured financing over AMP Securities.
rules.evidence: AMP warns all other Designated Persons against entering into or maintaining any margin lending arrangement over or in respect of AMP Securities

rules.detail: A hard 30 day buy to sell (or sell to buy) window measured from the last buy until a sell of a Security of that class or type. Successive buys or successive sells within 30 days are unrestricted. Carve-out for trading shares acquired on the exercise of options or the exercise or vesting of performance or share rights under a Share Plan.
rules.evidence: Designated Persons must not engage in short term trading (ie 30 days or less) in AMP Securities. The 30 days applies from the last time an AMP Security is bought until an AMP Security of that class or type is sold (or vice versa).

rules.detail: The 30 day rule applies only to Designated Persons.

clearance.approver: Head of Corporate Governance (or their delegate); the Group General Counsel for a notification by the Head of Corporate Governance
clearance.post_trade_to: Head of Corporate Governance (or their delegate), written confirmation of the Trade
clearance.post_trade_deadline: no later than 3 business days after effecting the Trade
clearance.evidence: The notification must be provided at least 2 business days prior to the proposed Trade being effected. Further, any proposed Trade so notified to the Head of Corporate Governance must be effected (even if not settled) within 5 business days of the date of notification. ... The Head of Corporate Governance (or their delegate) may direct the Designated Person who is proposing to Trade not to do so, or to impose conditions on the Trade in their discretion, and is not obliged to provide reasons.

clearance.approver: Clearance Officer: the Chairman of the Audit Committee for the Chairman of the Board; the Chairman of the Board for any other AMP Limited Director including the CEO; a committee of any two of the CEO, Group General Counsel and Group CFO for any other Designated Person
clearance.post_trade_to: Head of Corporate Governance (the Clearance Officer must promptly advise any clearance granted, and Group Corporate Governance keeps a record)
clearance.evidence: Any approval will be effective for 5 business days from the date on which it is given (or any other period specified) ... If a request is not approved or an approval is revoked, that fact must be kept confidential.

clearance.approver: Head of Corporate Governance, who then notifies the Chairman of the Board (or the Chairman of the Audit Committee where the notifier is the Chairman of the Board)
clearance.post_trade_to: AMP, notice of all changes in notifiable interests under the separate agreements between AMP and each Director (ASX Listing Rule 3.19A, s205G)
clearance.post_trade_deadline: as soon as reasonably possible and in any event within 3 business days of the trade being undertaken
clearance.evidence: Directors of AMP Limited must give AMP notice of all such changes as soon as reasonably possible and in any event within 3 business days of the trade being undertaken.
Additional restrictions apply to Trading by Designated Persons as set out in section 2 of this policy.

short_term.basis: 30 days from the last time an AMP Security is bought until an AMP Security of that class or type is sold (or vice versa); successive buys or successive sells are unrestricted
carve_outs: Trades in shares acquired on the exercise of options
Trades in shares acquired on the exercise or vesting of performance rights
Trades in shares acquired on the vesting of share rights under any Share Plan
short_term.evidence: Designated Persons must not engage in short term trading (ie 30 days or less) in AMP Securities.

exceptions.evidence: participation in a Share Plan. However, where AMP Securities granted under a Share Plan cease to be held under the terms of that plan, any Trades in those Securities must only occur in accordance with this policy
the acquisition of AMP Securities through a dividend reinvestment plan
the acquisition of AMP Securities through a share purchase plan available to any retail shareholders
the acquisition of AMP Securities or disposal of rights to AMP Securities through a rights issue
the acquisition or disposal of AMP Securities through the acceptance of a takeover offer, scheme of arrangement or equal access buy-back

Trades that result in no effective change to the beneficial interest in the AMP Securities (for example, transfers of AMP Securities already held into a superannuation fund or trust of which the Designated Person is a beneficiary)
subject to section 2.7, a disposal of AMP Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement

investing in, or Trading in units of or interests in, a fund or other scheme (other than a scheme investing primarily in AMP Securities) where the assets of the fund or other scheme are invested at the discretion of a third party
an off-market transaction in AMP Securities where no or only nominal consideration is given or received by the Designated Person or any Close Associate of that Designated Person
severe financial hardship where the sale of Securities is the only practical method of overcoming hardship
a requirement to Trade in Securities pursuant to a court order or a court enforceable undertaking
an overriding legal or regulatory requirement to transfer or accept a transfer of Securities.

Separate trading policies adopted for specified Business Units, such as for AMP Investments
AMP Share Plan rules (AMP Equity Incentive Plan, non-executive directors' share plan and successor or similar plans)

exemption_authority: Section 3: a Designated Person may apply in writing to the Head of Corporate Governance (or the Group General Counsel for the Head of Corporate Governance) to Trade during a black-out period in exceptional circumstances, decided by the relevant Clearance Officer within 5 business days on evidence that trading is the most reasonable course of action and a declaration of no Inside Information. The relief is expressly limited to exempting the person from section 2.2 black-out restrictions; it does not lift the section 1.7 hedging ban or the section 2.7 margin lending prohibition.
jurisdiction_overlays: Section 1.8: Directors and Employees working outside Australia or Trading in Securities in another jurisdiction must also comply with the laws of that jurisdiction
Corporations Act prohibition on Key Management Personnel and their closely related parties hedging unvested equity remuneration or vested equity subject to holding locks (recorded in section 1.7)

bespoke_clauses.clause: This prohibition ceases to apply in respect of any Equity Instrument acquired through a Share Plan from the time it is withdrawn from the plan, converted to an ordinary AMP share or converted to cash (whichever is the earliest).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The hedging ban is defined by plan custody rather than by vesting, so a collar becomes available over exactly the shares that have been withdrawn from the Share Plan and are held as ordinary AMP shares; the bank should evidence withdrawal or conversion before pricing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors of AMP Limited and members of the Executive Committee are prohibited from entering into or maintaining any margin lending arrangement over or in respect of AMP Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For the two most likely client groups the loan leg of a funded collar, secured over AMP shares, is very likely a margin lending arrangement 'in respect of AMP Securities' and is banned outright, with no clearance or exceptional circumstances route.

bespoke_clauses.clause: prohibited from entering into or maintaining any margin lending arrangement
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A person who becomes an AMP Limited director or ExCo member while a funded collar loan is outstanding must unwind it, so promotion or board appointment is an unwind trigger the facility documents must anticipate.

bespoke_clauses.clause: subject to section 2.7, a disposal of AMP Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights, for example, under a margin lending arrangement [is excepted from the black-out prohibition]
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: For a Designated Person who is not a Director or ExCo member, lender enforcement or physical settlement during a black-out period is an excepted Trade and does not breach the policy, which is unusually accommodating of secured lending mechanics.

bespoke_clauses.topic: no clearance for margin call sales
bespoke_clauses.clause: Clearance would not likely be granted under section 3 of this policy to sell AMP Securities during a black-out period to allow a Designated Person to comply with the terms of a margin lending arrangement.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The executive cannot rely on being allowed to sell into a black-out period to top up collateral, so any funded collar should be sized and margined so no discretionary top-up sale is ever required.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Head of Corporate Governance (or their delegate) may direct the Designated Person who is proposing to Trade not to do so, or to impose conditions on the Trade in their discretion, and is not obliged to provide reasons for any direction or condition.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Although 2.4 is framed as notification rather than approval, AMP retains an unreasoned veto, so collar entry, roll and unwind carry execution risk right up to the trade date.

bespoke_clauses.clause: a proposed Trade may only be effected on the second, third, fourth or fifth business day after notification.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Pricing and execution of the collar legs must be scheduled inside a four business day window opening two business days after notification, which constrains fixing dates and roll mechanics.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons must not engage in short term trading (ie 30 days or less) in AMP Securities. The 30 days applies from the last time an AMP Security is bought until an AMP Security of that class or type is sold (or vice versa).
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because AMP Securities include derivatives over AMP shares, entering and unwinding or rolling collar legs within 30 days risks breaching 2.8; tenor and roll dates should exceed 30 days.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Designated Persons must also take appropriate steps to ensure that their Close Associates only Trade in Securities in circumstances where the Designated Person themselves would be permitted to Trade under this policy.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar through a controlled trust, company or investment account does not avoid the black-out, notification, short selling or hedging restrictions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: This policy may also be specifically extended in writing by the CEO by specifying that Designated Persons are restricted from Trading in the Securities of other specified entities with which an AMP Group Company may have a relationship.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The restricted universe is not fixed to AMP Securities and can be broadened by CEO direction, which matters where the collar references a basket or a related listed entity.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Directors and Employees should ask themselves not only 'can we?', but 'should we?' ... How would it look if the transaction were reported on the front page of the newspaper?
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A funded collar by a senior executive is precisely the kind of transaction this test targets, so expect scrutiny and possible informal discouragement even where each leg is technically compliant.

summary: A funded collar is available only to a narrow group and only over shares that have left the Share Plan. Section 1.7 bans any hedging arrangement over shares, options, share rights and performance rights held in a Share Plan, vested or unvested, and lifts only once the instrument is withdrawn from the plan, converted to an ordinary AMP share or converted to cash, so the derivative legs can be written only over ordinary AMP shares held outside the plan. For those shares the put and call are expressly Trading in AMP Securities: a Designated Person must notify the Head of Corporate Governance in writing at least 2 business days ahead, execute on the second to fifth business day after notification, stay outside the 15 June and 15 December black-out periods and any Board or Market Disclosure Committee blackout, avoid the 30 day short term trading rule, and accept that the Head of Corporate Governance can veto or condition the trade without reasons. The loan leg is the blocker for the target clients: AMP Limited directors and Executive Committee members are absolutely prohibited from entering into or maintaining any margin lending arrangement over or in respect of AMP Securities, with no clearance or exceptional circumstances route, so a funded collar is not possible for them. For other Designated Persons the policy only warns against margin lending and expressly excepts a secured lender's enforcement sale from the black-out prohibition, so a funded collar is workable, subject to the caveat that clearance to sell into a black-out period to meet a margin obligation would not likely be granted.
